resolutions.researcher_notes: OPEC ASB 2012 Table 4.10 (p.75, 'Gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2011') lists 'Km–91.5/Brega', operator Sirte Oil, 92 miles, 36in, capacity 21,240,442 (1,000 scm/yr) among active transporting lines. Libya Herald (Apr 2026) confirms the same 'Kilometre 91 Complex'/'Line 36B' node on the Sirte Oil network is presently receiving and forwarding gas (new Zueitina Field-103 supply tied in there, then pumped onward through the coastal gas network) — status 'operating' is corroborated by two independent sources across different eras (2011 data; 2026 news), satisfying the 2+ independent test even though 'operating' isn't a literal token in either.

Both sources unambiguously describe a natural-gas trunkline: OPEC ASB Table 4.10 is titled 'Gas pipelines in OPEC Members'; Libya Herald describes gas being pumped from Zueitina Field 103 through the km-91 complex into the coastal gas network for domestic gas supply.

OPEC ASB 2012 Table 4.10 (p.75/pdf p.78), row 'Km–91.5/Brega', Sirte Oil, capacity 21,240,442 thousand scm/yr = 21.240442 bcm/yr — exact match to GEM's 21.24 bcm/y (verified via pdftotext -layout on the live PDF; the automated substring screen misses it because the PDF's text layer doesn't expose the comma-grouped digits as a contiguous string, but I read the extracted table directly). Also present, with the identical 92mi/36in/21,240,442 figures, in ASB 2010‑2011 (https://www.opec.org/assets/assetdb/asb-2010-2011.pdf, live but same content-screen limitation) — not counted as a second independent source since it's the same OPEC series reporting the same year's data. FLAG: later ASB editions (2013‑2015) split this same named segment 'Km–91.5/Brega' into TWO parallel lines (36in ≈ 7.75M scm/yr + 16in ≈ 0.26M scm/yr ≈ 8.01 bcm/yr combined for 2013), a materially different capacity than the 21.24 bcm/y carried in the 2011/2012 edition for the single 36in line. GEM's capacity value matches the earlier (2011/2012) single-line figure, not the later dual-line total — worth a look since GEM's Length and Diameter values (below) instead match the LATER dual-line description. Tier medium: one source series, with a cross-edition inconsistency noted rather than resolved.

OPEC ASB 2013 Table 4.10 lists 'Km–91.5/Brega' as two parallel lines of 57.04 miles each (Sirte Oil; 36in and 16in) — same editions from 2014/2015 show it as 'Km-91.5/Brega (2)' = '2 x 57' miles. 57.04 mi x 2 = 114.08 mi = 183.6 km, close to GEM's 184.00 km (small rounding/edition variance, not exact). This is the SAME underlying OPEC series as the Capacity ref above, not a second independent source — tier low/single-source, and flagged because it only approximately reproduces 184.00 (183.5–183.6 km range across the 2013–2015 editions I checked, never exactly 184). Could not find a non-OPEC source stating a length for this specific named segment; UNRESOLVED-adjacent but keeping REFS_ADDED since a real, verifiable OPEC table row does support a value in the right range.

GEM's combined '36, 16' in diameter matches OPEC ASB 2013–2015's description of 'Km–91.5/Brega' as two parallel lines, one 36in and one 16in (same segment name, same owner Sirte Oil). Separately, Libya Herald (Apr 2026) refers to the same km-91 node's line as 'Line 36B', consistent with a designated 36in line ('B') existing at this junction — an independent, current confirmation that a 36in line specifically is part of this node's infrastructure, corroborating the OPEC-sourced 36in component (the 16in component is OPEC-only).

Both StartCountryOrArea/EndCountryOrArea = Libya are trivially supported: OPEC ASB lists the segment under its 'Libya' country heading; Wikipedia's Sirte Oil Company article places the company and the Brega gas hub in Libya (Marsa Al Brega). No sub-national StartLocation/EndLocation is populated in the sheet to verify beyond country level.

OPEC ASB lists 'Sirte Oil' as owner/operator of this segment. Wikipedia's Sirte Oil Company article independently states SOC 'operat[es] under the state-owned National Oil Corporation (NOC)' as its subsidiary (no exact percentage given on either source). Together these support GEM's Owner1 = 'Libyan National Oil Corp' 100% as the ultimate parent, with Sirte Oil as the operating subsidiary — consistent with how GEM typically records ultimate ownership. Tier medium: two independent sources agree on the SOC→NOC relationship but neither states a numeric ownership percentage for this specific pipeline, so the '100%' figure itself is inferred rather than directly quoted.

P1872 (Km-91.5-Brega) and P1868 (Km-81.5-Brega) are NOT the same pipeline double-counted — OPEC ASB Table 4.10 (2010-2011/2012 editions) tabulates them as distinct rows with different upstream feeders, diameters, and capacities: 'Km–91.5/Brega' (36in, 92mi, cap 21.24 bcm/y, fed by 'Attahaddy/km-91.5' 30in) vs 'Km–81.5/Brega' (30in, 82mi, cap 8.50 bcm/y, fed by 'Sahel/km-81.5' and 'Intesar/Sahel' 30in lines). Both are real, separately-dimensioned trunks of the same Sirte-Basin-to-Brega gas gathering system that happen to share Brega as their common terminus — i.e. they are parallel corridors into the same hub, not one line recorded twice. GEM's separate P1867 'Attahaddy-km-91.5' and P1871 'Sahel-km-81.5' rows correspond to the respective upstream feeder segments in the same OPEC table, reinforcing that the '91.5' and '81.5' junctions are two distinct nodes on the network, each with its own feeder + Brega-bound trunk, not a single shared trunk. No evidence found that P1872 and P1868 should be merged or that either is a phantom duplicate of the other.
